log.text: Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Venusaur

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott and Mega Tyranitar immediately contest sun with Prankster Tailwind, Taunt, and Sand Stream while Rock Slide pressures Charizard and Venusaur. Gholdengo provides strong spread damage and status immunity; Milotic supplies rain control, Ice Beam, and Competitive punishment for Tauros.
decisions.notebook: Core plan: use Whimsicott/Tyranitar to contest Drought, with Prankster Tailwind or Taunt and Mega Tyranitar’s Sand Stream. Preserve Milotic as the safest rain pivot and Ice coverage option; Competitive punishes opposing Intimidate. Gholdengo is the preferred special attacker into Grass- and Fairy-adjacent pressure and benefits from Good as Gold against status. Consider Basculegion in later games when a dedicated rain offense is more valuable.

decisions.rationale: Lead Charizard + Raichu to Mega Evolve into sun while Fake Out can deny Whimsicott’s Tailwind. Venusaur converts sun into immediate speed pressure from the back, while Tauros is the dedicated Mega Tyranitar answer.
decisions.notebook: Primary mode: Mega Charizard Y establishes sun and enables Chlorophyll Venusaur. Raichu is valuable into Whimsicott for Fake Out, and can disrupt with Encore/Nuzzle afterward. Tauros-Paldea-Aqua is the direct answer to Tyranitar with Close Combat and provides Water pressure. Gholdengo has Good as Gold, so do not attempt status disruption into it; pressure it with Charizard Fire attacks or Kingambit Dark attacks when selected. Opponent’s listed Arcanine is Flash Fire, not Intimidate. Milotic is Competitive, so avoid switching Tauros in front of it unless the Special Attack boost is acceptable.

decisions.rationale: Tailwind acts before Charizard and establishes speed control. Mega Tyranitar Protects to block Raichu’s Fake Out and preserve the guaranteed spread Rock Slide KO on Mega Charizard next turn while setting sand over sun.
decisions.notebook: Prioritize Whimsicott Tailwind plus Mega Tyranitar’s Rock Slide into Charizard-based leads. Mega Tyranitar’s Rock Slide is a guaranteed OHKO on Mega Charizard Y even after spread reduction, while sun Heat Wave is manageable into Mega Tyranitar. Protect Mega Tyranitar on turn 1 when Raichu’s Fake Out can otherwise deny the knockout; preserve Milotic as the safest rain pivot and Ice-coverage option, and Gholdengo as the preferred special attacker into Grass/Fairy pressure.

decisions.rationale: Bring in Milotic as the safer pivot and preserve Gholdengo for later special-attacking pressure. Tyranitar should remain ready to use Rock Slide into Charizard once Fake Out pressure is no longer available.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott is gone for this game. Opposing Charizard-Y has revealed Heat Wave, and Raichu has revealed Fake Out; Raichu's Fake Out has been spent. Preserve Milotic as the preferred rain pivot and retain Gholdengo for later Grass/Fairy-oriented pressure. Mega Tyranitar remains the primary Charizard answer with Rock Slide.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve and Fake Out Whimsicott: Fake Out breaks its Sash and prevents Prankster Tailwind/Taunt this turn, while sun-boosted Heat Wave then reliably finishes it if it connects and chips Tyranitar. Removing Whimsicott is worth exposing Charizard to Rock Slide; Tauros can clean Tyranitar afterward.
decisions.notebook: Primary plan: Mega Charizard Y establishes sun for Chlorophyll Venusaur. Raichu is especially valuable versus Whimsicott: Fake Out breaks Focus Sash and denies its Prankster support for that turn; Encore/Nuzzle offer follow-up disruption. Tauros-Paldea-Aqua is the direct Tyranitar answer via Close Combat and Intimidate. Gholdengo has Good as Gold: do not use status moves into it; pressure with Charizard Fire damage. Opponent Arcanine is Flash Fire, not Intimidate. Milotic is Competitive: avoid bringing Tauros in front of it unless accepting its Special Attack boost. Tyranitar can Mega Evolve and reset sand after Charizard’s Drought depending on activation order.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Charizard: Mega Tyranitar's Rock Slide is a guaranteed KO if it connects, while Milotic's Hydro Pump provides a second KO chance if Rock Slide misses. Rain Dance is too slow to prevent an immediate SolarBeam, and protecting Milotic forfeits pressure.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott is gone for this game. Charizard-Y has revealed Heat Wave; Raichu has revealed Fake Out, which is spent. Preserve Milotic as the preferred rain pivot when practical, and retain Gholdengo for later Grass/Fairy-oriented pressure. Mega Tyranitar is the primary Charizard answer with Rock Slide.

decisions.rationale: Protect preserves Charizard from Tyranitar’s 4x Rock Slide and Milotic’s possible Hydro Pump while Raichu safely pressures Milotic first. Thunderbolt deals 36.6–64.7%, establishing range without risking a sand-charged Solar Beam.
decisions.notebook: Primary plan: Mega Charizard Y establishes sun for Chlorophyll Venusaur. Raichu is especially valuable versus Whimsicott: Fake Out breaks Focus Sash and denies its Prankster support for that turn; Encore/Nuzzle offer follow-up disruption. Tauros-Paldea-Aqua is the direct Tyranitar answer via Close Combat and Intimidate. Gholdengo has Good as Gold: do not use status moves into it; pressure with Charizard Fire damage. Opponent Arcanine is Flash Fire, not Intimidate. Milotic is Competitive: avoid bringing Tauros in front of it unless accepting its Special Attack boost. Tyranitar can Mega Evolve and reset sand after Charizard’s Drought depending on activation order. In sand, Charizard Solar Beam requires a charge turn; do not select it without sun or a protected setup line.

decisions.rationale: Milotic Protects to deny Raichu’s Thunderbolt and any SolarBeam pressure while Tyranitar uses Rock Slide, which is a guaranteed KO on Charizard even after spread reduction. This preserves Milotic as a future rain pivot and removes the primary weather threat.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott is unavailable for the remainder of Game 1. Charizard-Mega-Y has revealed Heat Wave and Protect; Raichu has revealed Fake Out and Thunderbolt, with Fake Out spent. Mega Tyranitar’s Rock Slide is the primary Charizard answer and can reliably KO it. Preserve Milotic for rain pivoting when practical, and retain Gholdengo for later Grass/Fairy-oriented pressure.

decisions.rationale: Preserve Charizard from Tyranitar’s immediate Rock Slide threat while Raichu, moving first, Encore-locks Milotic into its previously used Hydro Pump. Venusaur resists that attack and can exploit the constrained Milotic next turn; avoid Tauros because Intimidate would trigger Competitive.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 confirmed: Mega Tyranitar is Adamant with Rock Slide, Crunch, Low Kick, Protect; Milotic is Calm Competitive with Rain Dance, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Protect and Leftovers. Mega Tyranitar’s sand overrides Mega Charizard Y’s Drought on entry order. Raichu can act before both revealed foes and Encore Milotic after Hydro Pump to constrain it. Preserve Tauros’s Intimidate carefully around Milotic because Competitive boosts its SpA. Venusaur is the preferred pivot into a Hydro Pump lock; establish sun later for Chlorophyll and instant Solar Beam when Tyranitar is removed or weather is controlled.

decisions.rationale: Bring Charizard back to reset sun without re-triggering Tyranitar’s Sand Stream, immediately restoring Venusaur’s Chlorophyll pressure. Tauros would hand Milotic a Competitive boost on entry and is the less reliable pivot into this board.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 confirmed: Mega Tyranitar is Adamant with Rock Slide, Crunch, Low Kick, Protect; Milotic is Calm Competitive with Rain Dance, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Protect and Leftovers. Mega Tyranitar’s sand overrides Mega Charizard Y’s Drought on initial simultaneous Mega activation, but Charizard can later re-enter to establish sun while Tyranitar remains in play. Raichu can act before both revealed foes and Encore Milotic after Hydro Pump to constrain it. Preserve Tauros’s Intimidate carefully around Milotic because Competitive boosts its SpA. Venusaur is the preferred pivot into a Hydro Pump lock; establish sun later for Chlorophyll and instant Solar Beam when Tyranitar is removed or weather is controlled.

decisions.rationale: Switch Milotic to Gholdengo to escape the Encore-locked, reduced-success Protect and preserve the rain pivot. Mega Tyranitar uses Rock Slide, which reliably KOs Charizard-Mega-Y despite spread reduction, while retaining pressure on Venusaur.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott is unavailable in Game 1. Charizard-Mega-Y has revealed Heat Wave and Protect; Raichu revealed Fake Out and Thunderbolt, with Fake Out spent. Mega Tyranitar's Rock Slide is the primary Charizard answer. Preserve Milotic for a future rain pivot when practical, and retain Gholdengo for Grass/Fairy-oriented pressure.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur guarantees Sleep Powder resolves before Tyranitar can Rock Slide; disabling the immediate Charizard KO threat gives Solar Beam the best chance to remove weakened Milotic under sun. Even if Solar Beam falls short, Tyranitar’s sleep creates the strongest follow-up position.

Make It Rain guarantees the KO on Venusaur while also damaging Charizard; Rock Slide is a guaranteed KO on Charizard if Tyranitar wakes. This removes both immediate threats and maximizes the chance of winning despite Tyranitar’s sleep.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott is unavailable for Game 1. Mega Tyranitar’s Rock Slide is the primary answer to Mega Charizard Y and reliably KOs it from full shown HP. Preserve Milotic for a future Rain Dance pivot when practical. Retain Gholdengo for Grass/Fairy-oriented pressure. Charizard has revealed Heat Wave, Solar Beam, Air Slash, and Protect; Venusaur has revealed Sleep Powder and is an urgent fast threat under sun.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Giga Drain plus Solar Beam guarantees Mega Tyranitar’s removal across the calculated damage ranges, while Giga Drain also recovers Venusaur. Removing Tyranitar preserves sun control and prevents its Rock Slide from immediately threatening Charizard.

Shadow Ball guarantees the KO on Venusaur despite Gholdengo’s -2 Special Attack, removing the fastest sleep threat. Milotic should Hydro Pump Charizard for super-effective pressure; under sun it can KO from 54%, while Rain Dance gives up the immediate chance to remove Charizard.
decisions.notebook: Mega Tyranitar’s Rock Slide is the primary answer to Mega Charizard Y when Tyranitar is available. Preserve Milotic for Rain Dance pivots when practical, and retain Gholdengo for Grass/Fairy-oriented pressure.

decisions.rationale: Sleep Powder is the only way to deny Milotic’s likely Rain Dance before Charizard moves. In sun, spread Heat Wave guarantees the KO on 71% Gholdengo if it does not Protect; if it Protects, sleeping Milotic preserves the favorable position. Targeting Milotic directly risks Rain Dance causing Solar Beam to charge.
decisions.notebook: G1 revealed: Mega Tyranitar Adamant (Rock Slide/Crunch/Low Kick/Protect); Milotic Calm Competitive with Rain Dance/Hydro Pump/Ice Beam/Protect and Leftovers; Whimsicott Prankster with Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast; Gholdengo Modest Metal Coat with Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Recover/Protect and Good as Gold. Good as Gold blocks status moves, so do not target Gholdengo with Sleep Powder. Mega Tyranitar’s sand overrides simultaneous Charizard Y Drought; Charizard re-entry can restore sun later. Preserve Tauros Intimidate around Milotic: Competitive gives it a SpA boost. In sun, Charizard Heat Wave cleanly threatens Gholdengo while Venusaur can threaten Milotic; Milotic Rain Dance can interrupt instant Solar Beam if used before Charizard acts.

decisions.rationale: Gholdengo is fainted, so pass. Milotic is asleep and would be KOed by Venusaur’s Giga Drain if it does not protect; Protect works while asleep and avoids both likely attacks, preserving a chance to wake and reset weather later.
Venusaur is guaranteed to move before Milotic and Life Orb Giga Drain is a guaranteed KO from 40%, ending the game immediately. Solar Beam is redundant insurance if needed and also guaranteed to KO.
decisions.notebook: G1 revealed: Mega Tyranitar Adamant (Rock Slide/Crunch/Low Kick/Protect); Milotic Calm Competitive with Rain Dance/Hydro Pump/Ice Beam/Protect and Leftovers; Whimsicott Prankster with Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast; Gholdengo Modest Metal Coat with Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Recover/Protect and Good as Gold. Good as Gold blocks status moves, so do not target Gholdengo with Sleep Powder. Mega Tyranitar’s sand overrides simultaneous Charizard Y Drought; Charizard re-entry can restore sun later. Preserve Tauros Intimidate around Milotic: Competitive gives it a SpA boost. In sun, Charizard Heat Wave cleanly threatens Gholdengo while Venusaur threatens Milotic; Milotic Rain Dance can interrupt instant Solar Beam if used before Charizard acts. Venusaur’s Chlorophyll Speed guarantees it moves before this Milotic; Life Orb Giga Drain KOs Milotic from 40% across legal bulk.

reflections.summary: Lost because the four brought were poorly matched into sun: Venusaur’s Sleep Powder disabled Mega Tyranitar and then Milotic, while Charizard-Y’s Solar Beam and Heat Wave removed the remaining answers. Mega Tyranitar was still the right Mega choice for its Rock Slide pressure, but Milotic was too passive and vulnerable in this matchup.
reflections.adjustment: Replace Milotic with a reserve that pressures Venusaur or prevents Sleep Powder, and lead Whimsicott with Mega Tyranitar so Taunt can deny Venusaur’s sleep support while Tyranitar threatens Charizard immediately. Keep Mega Tyranitar as the evolved holder.
reflections.notebook: Opposing Charizard-Y/Venusaur sun uses Chlorophyll speed and repeated Sleep Powder to neutralize checks before dealing damage. Mega Tyranitar remains a strong Charizard answer, but cannot be treated as safe while Venusaur is active; provide Taunt, sleep prevention, or a direct Venusaur answer. Milotic’s Rain Dance plan is unreliable if Venusaur gets an early Sleep Powder, so avoid bringing it as the primary sun counter unless rain can be established proactively.

reflections.summary: Won because Mega Charizard Y’s sun enabled Venusaur’s speed and Charizard’s pressure, while Sleep Powder removed Tyranitar and Milotic long enough to finish the opposing core. The Charizard Y/Venusaur/Raichu/Tauros selection was suitable; Mega Y was the correct evolution, and Tauros was not needed after the three active contributors controlled the game.
reflections.adjustment: If this four repeats, keep the Charizard Y/Venusaur/Raichu core and Mega Evolve Charizard; prioritize preserving Raichu’s disruption for Whimsicott or a protected Milotic rather than relying solely on Sleep Powder. Do not bring Tauros into Milotic unless necessary, since Competitive punishes Intimidate.
reflections.notebook: G1: Opponent chose Whimsicott/Mega Tyranitar/Gholdengo/Milotic, leaving its Fire- and rain-sweeper options out. Mega Charizard Y plus Venusaur is a strong preview plan into this composition: sun enables Chlorophyll and pressures Gholdengo/Milotic. Raichu Encore can punish Milotic Protect and support the sun mode. Whimsicott has Prankster Tailwind, Taunt, Encore, and Moonblast; preserve disruption tools around it. Mega Tyranitar is Adamant with Rock Slide/Crunch/Low Kick/Protect. Milotic is Calm Competitive Leftovers with Rain Dance/Hydro Pump/Ice Beam/Protect; avoid casual Intimidate and respect Rain Dance disrupting Solar Beam. Gholdengo has Good as Gold, so Sleep Powder cannot target it.
